subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the conversation today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size Dedicated capacity and get you a formal quote:

Summary of your needs (from today's call)
- Deployment preference: Dedicated capacity (customer-managed pool in our shared infra) with possibility to migrate to Private VPC later.
- Primary workload: conversational assistant + batch reranking for search results.
- Traffic pattern: steady baseline with predictable daytime peak and short bursts during releases.

Key sizing questions for you (please confirm):
1) TPS targets (inference requests per second): what is your expected steady-state TPS and peak burst TPS?
2) Concurrency: how many concurrent sessions do you expect to hold active KV caches for?
3) Token mix: average prompt length and average completion length (tokens) and % of requests that are short vs long.
4) Model & latency targets: any hard P95 latency SLO (e.g., <300ms) and preferred model family (we can map to H100 vs A100 / quantized variants).

Initial docs attached: capacity_estimate.xlsx (blank sizing sheet) — fill the TPS/concurrency/token columns and I'll run an infra estimate.

Next steps I propose:
- You send answers to the four questions above this week.
- We run a quick sizing exercise and propose GPU mix (H100 vs A100), slot counts, and expected cost.
- Follow-up call with our Solutions Engineer to validate KV/cache assumptions and test plan.

If it helps, here are example guidance numbers we use internally for planning (ballpark):
- H100 (1:1 model): ~300–600 TPS for small 4–8k token contexts depending on batching.
- A100 (8-bit quant): better cost-per-token for very large contexts but higher latency variance.
- Typical medium production: 200–500 steady TPS, bursts to 1k–2k (require autoscale/burst lanes).

Thanks — if you can fill out the sheet or reply inline, I’ll get a concrete sizing and a draft SOW ready.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: capacity_estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@fintechco.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the clear summary and the template. Answering inline below. I attached our security questionnaire as well.

1) TPS targets:
- Steady-state TPS: ~450 TPS (production peak during business hours).
- Burst TPS: up to ~1,200 TPS for short windows (1–5 minutes) during product releases.

2) Concurrency:
- We expect ~120 concurrent active sessions (each holds a KV cache for a user session).
- Additionally ~300 short-running stateless requests (e.g., embeddings/rerank) that do not maintain KV cache.

3) Token mix:
- Average prompt: 80 tokens (customer messages + context).
- Average completion: 420 tokens (detailed assistant responses).
- Distribution: ~60% long (>300 tokens), ~40% short (<150 tokens).

4) Model & latency targets:
- Preferred model latency: P95 < 550ms for interactive flows.
- We're open to model family that matches price/perf; latency is more important than minimal cost.
- We prefer H100-backed instances if that materially improves latency.

Additional notes:
- We will want an autoscale policy that supports fast bursts (scale to burst lanes) and a fallback to a cheaper quantized variant if capacity constrained.
- Security: we will need SOC2 evidence and a short discussion about token retention/purge policies.

Attached: FINTECH_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (PDF stub)

Next steps: we can do the Solutions Engineer call next Wednesday (28 Jul) at 10am ET. Let me know if that works for your team.

Thanks,
Sam Taylor
Head of Product — Conversational AI | FintechCo
sam.taylor@fintechco.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Sam —

Perfect, this is very helpful. Based on the numbers you provided I'll do an initial capacity run with two scenarios:

Scenario A (latency-optimized, H100 primary)
- GPUs: H100-backed slots (N slots) to meet 450 TPS steady and 1,200 TPS bursts with autoscale lanes.
- Concurrency sizing: reserve ~140 KV cache slots to cover concurrent sessions + buffer.
- Estimated P95: ~350–450ms on H100 for your token mix (depends on batching aggressiveness).

Scenario B (cost-optimized, mixed quantized)
- GPUs: mix of A100-quantized for baseline and H100 for latency-critical routes.
- Autoscale policy: shift non-interactive rerank/embeddings to lower-cost pool.

Requested items from your side before solution call:
- Confirm that 1,200 TPS burst windows are typically <=5 minutes (you confirmed, but I want it on record).
- Any strict retention/purge windows for tokens (we will propose 0 retention for PII inputs by default unless you request otherwise).

I attached a draft SOW (minor placeholders for pricing) — draft_SOW_Redwood_v1.pdf. I’ll hand this to Marissa to prepare a quote.

Can you confirm the Wednesday 28 Jul 10am ET slot? I’ll invite our Solutions Engineer (will be on the call to validate cache behavior and test plan).

Best,
Aditya

Attachment: draft_SOW_Redwood_v1.pdf (PDF stub)
